name: Heat Take
job: List the author's opinions from mild to loco, with the heat shown as a five-pip meter and a word, so the reader can tell a safe take from a provocative one without a colour ladder.

anatomy.role: One take a row, hairlines between rows only
Five pips, filled to the level, then the word (Mild, Medium, Caliente, Fuego, Loco)
One or two sentences in the author's voice

states.name: Mild to loco
states.note: All five levels in one ink: the pip count carries the heat.

states.name: Phone width
states.note: Below 38rem the meter sits above its take.

use_when: The author's own opinions, ranked by how far they push.
A recap where the reader wants the blunt version after the evidence.
avoid_when: Do not colour the heat green to red: in ARCS green means proven and red means failed, and a take is neither.
Do not mix observed facts into takes; facts belong in 57 Ledger row or 59 Claim check.
access: The word names the level; the pips are `aria-hidden`, so a screen reader hears Caliente, not five dots.
No colour carries meaning here, so it reads the same in greyscale and in print.
